lead: Test build 0.8.27 (CI run 39230793499). New in this round, from checking the firmware findings against the code: (1) host automation gets its own time stamp at its block time, so it lands where the DAW put it, above all on Windows; one stamp per block keeps the byte budget for the notes (E261, E264); (2) a patch change or project load while playing counts against the byte budget as a bounded debt (E261); (3) the plug-in never sends the multi header parameters 0-3 or status F4 (rule 2, issue #7); (4) on Windows the audio streamer gets the Linux protection against the 48 kHz state after a wake, and both brokers also send the Virus' own 44.1 kHz setting next to the retry (E241, E257); (5) the macOS audio input fills skipped Core Audio cycles with silence, the cause of the late notes after a Mac export (E249); (6) the Linux installer names missing Control Center libraries (issue #9). The short smoke test was skipped on purpose, so the core items run on every system. The real PC is last and optional. Mark each item, add a note where something looks different, then copy the results at the bottom into the chat.
rules: Never store a patch on the Virus: patch changes in this round only load patches into the edit buffer.
Order: Linux first (the Virus is on this PC), then the Windows 11 VM, then macOS, then the real PC if you want it. Close the DAW before the Virus moves.

sections.title: Linux
sections.where: REAPER via pw-jack, Virus on this PC
prep: Claude installs 0.8.27 from the CI run (replaces the dev build in ~/.vst3 and the broker) and checks that install.sh reports no missing library. Logging is on. Restart REAPER if it was open.
Timing project: the 16th-note clip (native/tools/timing-16ths-120bpm.mid) on part 1, a short percussive patch.
notes: Exports in REAPER: File > Render, Source Master mix, Render speed Full-speed offline, into work/timing/ with the item's name.
LC5 (sleep): if the Virus comes back silent or loud, stop and note it. Claude then reads the broker log for the new line with global 73 00 10 00.

items.title: Two parts play the same note at the same time
steps: Load the same short percussive patch on part 1 and part 2. Set part 1's output to USB 1 and part 2's output to USB 2.
Copy the 16th-note clip to a second MIDI track on channel 2.
Route the plug-in's Out 1 and Out 2 to two tracks and render them as stems to work/timing/L1-out1.wav and work/timing/L1-out2.wav.
items.expect: both stems have all notes on the grid. Claude compares their onsets: the question is whether the Virus' two DSPs add an offset of about 6 ms between parts (E245, E263).

items.title: Notes stay on the grid while automation runs
steps: On the timing track, automate Cutoff, Resonance and Filter Envelope Amount of part 1 with fast curves (an LFO-like shape, a few cycles per bar) for the whole clip.
Play it once and listen; then render to work/timing/L2.wav.
items.expect: the filter moves audibly while every note plays, no sync error page, no hanging note. Claude measures the file: all notes on the grid, jitter as in LC3.

items.title: Patch change while playing
steps: Add a second track that plays the 16th-note clip on part 2 (any patch).
Loop bars 1-4. While it plays, pick a different patch for part 1 from LOAD about five times, a few seconds apart.
Record the plug-in's output into an audio track while you do it, and save the take as work/timing/L3.wav.
items.expect: part 2 keeps playing in time through every patch change (at most a short gap on part 1 itself), no sync error page. Claude measures part 2's notes in the file.

sections.title: Windows 11 VM
sections.where: win11 VM, Ableton Live 11, Virus attached by Claude
prep: Claude installs 0.8.27 silently and attaches the Virus (ask in the chat).
Timing set: the 16th-note clip on part 1, a short percussive patch.
notes: Windows sends notes further ahead than Linux and macOS, so the automation timing matters most here (E261).

items.title: Automation lands where Live puts it
steps: Give the clip a clip envelope for part 1's Cutoff as a square wave: 0 for the first half of each bar, 127 for the second half.
Play it once and listen; then export to Desktop\W1.wav.
items.expect: the sound turns bright exactly on beat 3 of each bar and dark on beat 1, never a 16th early or late; all notes on the grid. Claude measures onsets and the brightness steps.

items.title: Patch change while playing
steps: Add a second MIDI track with the 16th-note clip on part 2.
Loop bars 1-4. While it plays, pick a different patch for part 1 from LOAD about five times, a few seconds apart.
items.expect: part 2 keeps playing in time through every patch change, no sync error page.

sections.title: macOS
prep: Claude pushes the package; install with sudo installer -pkg "$HOME/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.27-mac/TI-Revive-0.8.27-mac/TI Revive.pkg" -target /. Virus on the Mac.
Claude puts diag.on and klog.on in the plug-in's folder and renames the old diag.log.
Timing set: the 16th-note clip on part 1, a short percussive patch.
notes: MC3 is this round's main Mac check: before 0.8.27 the notes came late after an export until the Virus was switched off and on (E243, E249).

items.title: Play right after an export
steps: Right after MC3, without switching the Virus off, play the clip again in Live and record the plug-in's output into an audio track for 30 s.
items.expect: notes are on time after the export, no sync error page. Claude checks diag.log: the delay K is the same before and after, and the stats line shows filled > 0 during the export.

items.title: Notes stay on the grid while automation runs
steps: Automate Cutoff, Resonance and Filter Envelope Amount of part 1 with fast curves for the whole clip.
Play it once and listen; then export to ~/Downloads/M2.wav.
items.expect: the filter moves audibly while every note plays, no sync error page. Claude measures the file.

sections.title: Real Windows PC (optional, last)
sections.where: this PC booted into Windows, one self-contained session
prep: Install TI-Revive-0.8.27-setup.exe from the CI run's artifacts (Claude says where to get it before you reboot). Logging on: an empty file diag.on in the plug-in's folder.

items.title: Automation lands where Live puts it
steps: The W1 set: square-wave Cutoff envelope, 0 then 127 in each bar. Export to Desktop\B1.wav and copy it to a USB stick or the Linux side.
items.expect: the sound turns bright on beat 3 and dark on beat 1 of each bar, all notes on the grid.
